summary.text: A 51-year-old male patient who had undergone laparoscopic partial gastrectomy for early gastric cancer, and had been given intravenous cefazolin for 2 days preventively, suddenly developed a high-grade fever (over 39 °C) and severe diarrhea 5 days after the surgery. Oral vancomycin, Lac-B (probiotics) and extracellular fluid were administered immediately because CDAC or methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus-associated enteritis was empirically suspected, and CDAC was diagnosed by confirming toxin A in his feces.

Twenty-four hours after the onset the patient developed septic shock requiring vasopressor agents and MODS composed of DIC and acute renal failure. When he was transferred to the ICU his APACHE II score was 22, estimating a 42.4 % risk of hospital death, and Table 1 gives his vital signs and laboratory data at that time, including body temperature 40 °C, heart rate 150/min, urine output 5 ml/h, serum creatinine 5.21 mg/dl and C-reactive protein 24.2 mg/dl.

Clinical and radiological findings showed no colonic perforation or toxic megacolon, so invasive surgery such as subtotal colectomy was avoided, although prompt surgical treatment to remove the septic sources was recommended, and he was treated with polymyxin B hemoperfusion (PMX-HP) to improve septic shock and recombinant human thrombomodulin (rhTM) to control DIC.

In the first 6 h after starting both treatments his systolic blood pressure improved, the vasopressor requirement decreased and body temperature dropped by approximately two degrees, and septic shock was dramatically improved 24 h after the treatments. Three days after the treatments, severe inflammation and DIC improved. Four cycles of CHDF were necessary for ARF, a temporary platelet decline was controllable with platelet transfusion, MODS did not progress further and the APACHE II score decreased daily.

Clinically moderate diarrhea and a mild fever were observed but his general condition improved, consecutive toxin A tests except the first were negative, and neither endotoxemia nor bacteremia was observed. Five days after the treatments the patient overcame fulminant CDAC, and the authors report the patient’s survival among the excellent outcomes.

ambiguities.issue: Empiric suspicion of CDAC or methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus-associated enteritis

evidence.quote: we empirically suspected that these symptoms were due to CDAC or methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus-associated enteritis
A diagnosis of CDAC was rapidly made by confirming the presence of toxin A in his feces.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: The either-or suspicion does not establish MRSA-associated enteritis; CDAC is recorded from the toxin A confirmation and no MRSA infection is stated.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase the onset in "24 h after the onset" is not defined in its sentence; the preceding sentences describe the sudden fever and diarrhea 5 days after the surgery

evidence.quote: 24 h after the onset the patient developed septic shock requiring vasopressor agents and MODS composed of DIC and acute renal failure (ARF)
5 days after the surgery suddenly developed a high-grade fever (over 39 °C) and severe diarrhea

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer an absolute time of onset, the time of ICU transfer, or hours between the surgery and the septic shock beyond the stated 5 days and 24 h.

evidence.quote: 24 h after the onset the patient developed septic shock requiring vasopressor agents and MODS composed of DIC and acute renal failure (ARF)

article_limitations: Single case report; the course is told in prose with one table of values at the time of ICU transfer and four chart figures of the clinical course.

Table 1 is the only tabulated set of values and has one time point; repeated measurements exist only as plotted points in Figs. 1 to 4, which are pixel content recorded in the visual review and not as facts.
The radiological findings behind the exclusion of colonic perforation and toxic megacolon, and the number, timing and doses of PMX-HP and rhTM treatments, are not described in the text.
Four cycles of CHDF and platelet transfusion are stated as necessary or controllable, so their action is recorded as unknown rather than completed.
Table 1 labels Symbolic blood pressure and Median blood pressure and the PaO2 footnote expansion are kept as printed.
Authors’ mechanistic speculation, literature statements and general recommendations in the abstract, discussion and conclusions are not patient facts and are not recorded.
Figure day axes and treatment lanes are not defined in the captions; no day-to-hour conversion is made.
